instructor.credentials: E-RYT 500 • 18 Years Devotion • Somatic Experiencing Practitioner
instructor.quote: “Yoga is not about touching your toes; it is about what you discover on the way down.”
instructor.bio1: Elena began her study along the banks of the Ganges in Rishikesh before deepening her craft through somatic physiology and therapeutic trauma work in Zurich. Arte was conceived as an antidote to performance-driven, athletic yoga.
instructor.bio2: Her methodology pairs classical alignment with soft neurological inquiry. Every cue invites you to cultivate intimacy with sensation, unravel habitual holding patterns, and return home to an unhurried mind.

testimonials.title: Sangha Reflections

About.metaDescription: Elena Vance, founder of Arte Yoga Studio: lineage, teaching philosophy and a personal letter to the practitioner.

hero.title: Guiding you back to your natural cadence of breath and stillness.
hero.body: I founded Arte Yoga Studio as an architectural refuge from the relentless pace of modern life — a physical and digital haven where movement is stripped of performance and restored to sacred self-inquiry.
hero.portraitAlt: Elena Vance, founder of Arte Yoga Studio

lineage.title: Rooted in rigor, softened by compassion.
lineage.body: Elena’s teaching bridges classical Eastern discipline with Western trauma-informed neurobiology, offering an authentic sanctuary for modern nervous systems.
story: My journey began over fifteen years ago in high-intensity classical ashtanga shalas. While the fire of discipline shaped my inner architecture, I witnessed countless practitioners — including myself — trade nervous system regulation for structural contortion. True yoga was never meant to be an aesthetic conquest.

A decade spent studying precision biomechanics alongside renowned Iyengar masters unraveled my approach to form: alignment is not about looking flawless from the outside, but feeling resonant and structurally sovereign from within.

Integrating somatic resolution practices and polyvagal theory transformed Arte from an exercise studio into a true refuge for the nervous system. Here, we invite the subtle body to exhale its stored hypervigilance. We honor the threshold between exertion and stillness.
lineage.quote: “The pose does not demand that you reshape your humanity to fit its geometry. Rather, the geometry yields, cradling the exact truth of who you are today.”

milestones.title: Foundation in Mysore
milestones.body: Immersive primary and intermediate Ashtanga series under traditional lineage masters, developing unwavering discipline and daily breath cadence.

milestones.title: Precision & Props
milestones.body: A deep dive into Iyengar props, structural integration, and restorative postures that invite profound neuromuscular release.

milestones.title: Somatic Synthesis
milestones.body: Trauma-informed polyvagal awareness woven into daily sequencing, so each movement communicates safety to the autonomic nervous system.

milestones.title: Arte Yoga Studio
milestones.body: Guiding an international digital community alongside seasonal in-person retreats centered on quiet longevity.

pillars.title: Four Pillars of Our Teaching
pillars.body: Every sequence, breath practice, and silent sit we curate is anchored firmly in four immovable principles.
pillars.label: Pillar {n}

items.title: Breath as Anchor
items.body: We never sacrifice respiratory smoothness for physical extension. The diaphragm is our compass, telling us whether to advance or soften.

items.title: Sustainable Alignment
items.body: Precise geometry rooted in joint longevity. We build postures from the ground up, honoring bone architecture over visual performance.

items.title: The Art of Pausing
items.body: Stillness is where integration happens. In unhurried transitions and deliberate rests, the body has space to absorb the medicine of motion.

items.title: Living Practice Off-Mat
items.body: Equanimity forged on the mat is tested in daily relationships, work, and unexpected friction. We practice to show up more softly and bravely for the world.

studio.title: An altar of linen, limestone, and unadorned light.
studio.body: Our physical space in the coastal hills was shaped to quiet sensory overwhelm. Every material was chosen for its grounding honesty.

hall.title: Acoustic hush & eastern sunlight
hall.body: Curved lime plaster diffuses sound, so Elena’s spoken cues land softly without amplification.
hall.alt: Sunlit practice hall with arched windows, oak floors and linen bolsters

linen.title: Tactile materiality
linen.alt: Undyed linen bolster on warm sandstone tile

tea.title: Silent tea commons
tea.alt: Ceramic tea bowls on a low wooden table beside a single branch

letter.title: From Elena’s desk
paragraphs: Dear traveler, whether you step into our physical studio with salt-laden hair or roll out your mat in the corner of your bedroom thousands of miles away, I want to release you from an invisible burden: you do not need to arrive here already calm.

You are permitted to arrive disoriented, tight-shouldered, exhausted from holding the architecture of your family or career together. Yoga is not a trophy reserved for the already peaceful. It is the kiln in which our fractures are tenderly attended to.

I do not consider myself a guru. I am simply a practitioner who has walked the path of somatic listening long enough to recognize the signposts. I will never ask you to perform for me. My only commitment is to hold a safe perimeter around your practice so you can unbind your breath, trust your gravity, and remember the quiet truth that has always lived underneath your hurry.
Take your time. Drink a cup of warm water. When you are ready, I will be here waiting at the threshold.

items.q: Is this practice suitable for beginners or recovering bodies?
items.a: Yes. Elena designs each sequence with non-hierarchical modifications. The restorative, breath and mobility practices are especially suited to joint sensitivity, past injuries, or a depleted nervous system.

items.q: How does the digital sanctuary differ from in-person retreats?
items.a: The digital sanctuary gives daily on-demand access to the full practice library and guided programs, with reflections shared alongside each practice. In-person retreats offer silent immersion and personal postural adjustments.

items.q: What props will I need to practice alongside Elena?
items.a: A firm mat, two cork or foam blocks, one woven blanket, and a cotton strap are ideal. For restorative practices a bolster helps, though household pillows and rolled towels work beautifully.

privacy.title: What we keep, and why
privacy.lede: Arte is a small studio, not an advertising business. We collect what a practice library needs to work, and nothing we cannot explain to you in a sentence.
privacy.noticeBody: This policy describes what the application does today, written by the people building it. It has not been reviewed by a lawyer and is not legal advice. Have it reviewed before Arte opens to the public.

sections.heading: What we collect
paragraphs: Everything below is something you gave us or something the app recorded because you asked it to.
items: Your account: name, email address, and a password that is stored only as a cryptographic hash — we never see it.
Your preferences: the practice rhythm you chose at sign-up, your language, and whether you asked for the newsletter.
Your practice: which practices you saved, which you marked complete, how many minutes they ran, and the programs you follow.
Your reflections: what you write under a practice or in the community circle, including notes you mark private.
Your sessions: a sign-in token, and the IP address and browser your session was opened from, so you can be kept signed in and we can spot a stolen session.
Notifications: if you turn them on, the address your browser gives us to deliver a push message.

sections.heading: What we do not collect
paragraphs: There are no advertising or analytics trackers in Arte. We do not buy data about you, sell data about you, or build a profile for anyone else.
We never see your payment details. Payments are not live yet; when they are, a payment provider will handle your card and we will only be told whether a membership is active.

sections.heading: Who can see your reflections
paragraphs: A reflection posted to the circle is visible to every signed-in member, under your name.

A reflection marked private is hidden from other members — but your instructor can read it. That is deliberate: a private note is how you ask your instructor something without the circle watching. Please do not use it for anything you would not want your instructor to read.

sections.heading: Where it is stored
paragraphs: Your data lives in a Postgres database hosted by Neon in the United States. Sign-in is handled in-house by Better Auth rather than an identity company.
If you sign in with Google or GitHub, that provider tells us your name, email address and avatar. They learn that you signed in to Arte. We never receive your password for those accounts.
Push notifications travel through the push service your browser vendor runs — Google for Chrome, Mozilla for Firefox, Apple for Safari. They carry the message; they do not have your account.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Your account and practice history stay until you delete them. Expired sessions and dead notification addresses are cleared automatically.

You can delete your account from your profile at any time. That removes your account, membership record, saved practices, completions and reflections. It cannot be undone, and we cannot restore it for you afterwards.

sections.heading: Your choices
paragraphs: You do not have to ask us for any of this — it is all in the app.
items: Change your name, rhythm or newsletter preference in your profile.
Turn notifications off from the bell in the header, or in your browser's site settings.
Delete a reflection yourself, at any time.
Delete your whole account from your profile.

sections.heading: Children
paragraphs: Arte is meant for adults. We do not knowingly keep accounts for children under 16. If you believe a child has an account here, write to us and we will remove it.

sections.heading: Changes, and getting in touch
paragraphs: If this policy changes in a way that affects you, we will say so in the app rather than quietly editing this page.
Questions about your data, or a request we have not built a button for yet, can go to the studio directly.

terms.title: Terms of practice
terms.lede: The agreement between you and Arte: what we offer, what we ask of you, and what we cannot promise.
terms.noticeBody: Arte is a video practice library, not medical care. The health and safety section below is the part that matters most. These terms are also a working draft and have not been reviewed by a lawyer.

sections.heading: Health and safety
paragraphs: Elena is a yoga teacher, not your doctor. Nothing in Arte is medical advice, diagnosis or treatment, and no practice here is prescribed for a condition.
Talk to a qualified clinician before you begin, especially if you are pregnant, recovering from injury or surgery, or living with a heart, joint, blood-pressure or neurological condition.

You practise unsupervised, and nobody can see you. Work within the range your body offers today, use the props a practice asks for, and come out of any shape that produces pain, dizziness or breathlessness. Stop and seek help if something is wrong.

sections.heading: Your account
paragraphs: Keep your password to yourself and your account to yourself. You are responsible for what happens under your sign-in, so tell us promptly if you think someone else has it.
One account is one person. Please do not share a membership.

sections.heading: Membership and payment
paragraphs: Membership opens the full library, the programs and the community circle. Some practices stay open to everyone.

Payments are not live yet. Nothing in Arte charges a card today, and any membership you hold has been granted rather than purchased. When real billing arrives, the price, the renewal date and how to cancel will be stated plainly before you are asked for anything.
When billing does begin: a membership renews until you stop it, cancelling keeps your access until the end of the period you have paid for, and we will not change a price without telling you first.

sections.heading: What you may do with the practices
paragraphs: Your membership is a personal licence to stream the practices for yourself. It is not a licence to download, re-upload, screen publicly, or teach from the recordings.
The videos, writing, photography and the Arte name belong to the studio.

sections.heading: What you write here
paragraphs: Your reflections remain yours. By posting one you let us show it in the app to the people its visibility allows.
The circle is a place for practice, not for promotion, abuse, or anyone else's private business. We may remove a reflection or close an account that makes the circle unsafe.

sections.heading: What we cannot promise
paragraphs: Arte is offered as it is. We cannot promise that every video plays on every device, that the service is never interrupted, or that a practice will produce a particular result in your body.
To the extent the law allows, the studio is not liable for injury or loss arising from your use of the practices. The safety section above is not a formality.

sections.heading: Ending it
paragraphs: You can delete your account whenever you like, from your profile.
We may close an account that breaks these terms. If we do, we will tell you why.

sections.heading: Changes
paragraphs: These terms will change as Arte grows — most obviously when real payments begin. Material changes will be announced in the app, not slipped quietly into this page.

ethics.title: Ethics and lineage
ethics.lede: Not a legal document — the commitments the studio holds itself to, and how to tell us when we fall short of them.
ethics.noticeBody: Yoga is a living tradition from South Asia, carried for thousands of years before any of us arrived. Teaching it online is a privilege borrowed from that lineage, not a product we invented.

sections.heading: Respect for the tradition
paragraphs: We use Sanskrit names because they carry meaning, and we try to say what they mean rather than decorating a class with them.
Arte teaches āsana, prāṇāyāma and stillness as practices of attention. We do not present them as a religion you must adopt, nor strip them of where they come from to make them easier to sell.

sections.heading: Scope of practice
paragraphs: A yoga teacher's job is to teach movement and breath. It is not to diagnose, to treat, or to replace a therapist.
Where a practice touches something clinical — injury, pregnancy, grief, trauma — we will say plainly that it is not treatment and point you towards someone qualified.

sections.heading: Consent and autonomy
paragraphs: You are the authority on your own body. Every cue in a practice is an invitation you may decline, and modifications are offered as equals rather than as the lesser version.
Nobody is watching you practise. There is no streak you must protect and no attendance anyone is marking.

sections.heading: Who this is for
paragraphs: Every body, age, size, gender and ability is welcome here. Where a practice assumes something — wrists that bear weight, the floor being reachable — we try to say so and offer another way in.
Persian and English are treated as equals in this app, not as an original and a translation.

sections.heading: Honesty about money
paragraphs: Prices are shown plainly, with no artificial scarcity, countdown timers or dark patterns pushing you towards a plan.
Some practices stay open to everyone, always. If the price is a genuine barrier for you, write to the studio — that conversation is welcome.

sections.heading: Honesty about the technology
paragraphs: We collect what the practice library needs and nothing for advertising. Where the app does something you might not expect — an instructor being able to read a private reflection, for instance — we say so in the privacy policy rather than burying it.
When something here is not finished, the app says so rather than implying otherwise.

sections.heading: Raising a concern
paragraphs: If a practice, a cue, or something in the circle felt wrong, tell the studio. A concern about conduct goes straight to Elena and will be answered personally.
Getting it wrong is survivable; not hearing about it is worse.

NotFound.title: This page is not here
NotFound.body: The link may be old, or the practice may have been renamed. The library is still where you left it.
